gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a price for a full 60 kWh system. Today on the maker stores, a 61.44 kWh EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X costs $26,691 at 12 kW, and a 61.44 kWh Anker SOLIX E10 costs $29,092 at 15.36 kW. The only real 60 kW unit ChatGPT showed, the Sol-Ark 60K, runs on 277/480 V three-phase power and costs $15,600 for the inverter alone.
standout_why: I compared against the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra product pages ChatGPT cited (us.ecoflow.com/products/delta-pro-ultra and its variants) and the DELTA Pro Ultra X specs page (ecoflow.com/us/delta-pro-ultra-x/specs). They list bundle prices or maximum capacity (61.44 kWh per inverter, 36 kW across 3 inverters), but none adds up the cost of a 60 kWh build. ChatGPT's own answer says only 'a 60kWh system costs more'. None of ChatGPT's results covers the Anker E10 or Sol-Ark, and none gives a price for any rival at 60 kWh.
decides: If the shopper means 60 kWh, this confirms the DELTA Pro Ultra X as the cheapest plug-in route at $26,691. The Anker E10 costs $2,401 more for the same 61.44 kWh but gives 15.36 kW of rated output instead of 12 kW. If the shopper means 60 kW of output, no 120/240 V home system on these lists gets there: the DPU X stops at 36 kW with 3 inverters. The Sol-Ark 60K is a 277/480 V three-phase commercial inverter that ships without batteries. Our F3800 Plus tops out at 53.8 kWh and 12 kW, so it can't reach 60 kWh at all.

findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Whole-Home Backup Power
findings.note: Arithmetic: $7,899 bundle (1 inverter + 2 batteries) + 8 × $2,349 extra battery = $26,691. That gives 10 × 6.144 = 61.44 kWh, the most one inverter takes, or about $434 per kWh. It does not include a Smart Home Panel 3 or gateway. Adding 2 more inverters for 36 kW is +2 × $3,799 = $34,289. Whether 10 batteries can be split across 3 inverters is my assumption; I did not check it.
